steps.tx: The **EXTRIP** 2015 criteria for **lithium toxicity** recommend **hemodialysis** when impaired kidney function coexists with a level above **4.0** mmol/L, or when seizures or life-threatening dysrhythmias occur at any level. A level above **5.0** mmol/L is a suggested indication. Older handbooks used **2.5** mmol/L plus **neurologic manifestations**, a cutoff EXTRIP replaced.

steps.tx: **Methanol poisoning** produces severe high anion gap acidosis and visual injury via alcohol dehydrogenase metabolism to **formic acid**, which inhibits cytochrome oxidase to cause **optic papillitis** and bilateral **putaminal necrosis**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Ethylene glycol** poisoning generates toxic **glycolic acid** and **oxalic acid**, causing severe metabolic acidosis and extensive precipitation of **calcium oxalate** monohydrate crystals throughout renal tubules, presenting with acute tubular necrosis. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Ethylene Glycol
points: Toxic metabolites: Glycolic acid and oxalic acid
Urinary crystals: Dumbbell and envelope calcium oxalate
Target organ injury: Acute tubular necrosis and renal failure
Specific adjunct: Thiamine and pyridoxine cofactors

right.title: Methanol
points: Toxic metabolites: Formaldehyde and formic acid

steps.tx: **Fomepizole**, or **4-methylpyrazole**, administered as a **15** mg/kg loading dose, competitively inhibits **alcohol dehydrogenase** to block toxic metabolite generation in toxic alcohol poisoning, paired with immediate **hemodialysis** for severe acidemia with pH below **7.15**. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Severe **salicylate** or **aspirin toxicity** is treated with emergent **hemodialysis** when serum levels exceed **90** mg/dL, or **6.5** mmol/L, in acute poisoning, or above **60** mg/dL in chronic poisoning with altered mental status or acidemia. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **EXTRIP** recommendations for **metformin-associated lactic acidosis**, designated as **MALA**, endorse prompt intermittent hemodialysis for severe refractory lactic acidosis when blood **lactate** exceeds **20** mmol/L or pH drops to **7.00** or lower. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
steps.say: EXTRIP recommendations for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, designated as MALA, endorse prompt intermittent hemodialysis for severe refractory lactic acidosis when blood lactate exceeds 20 mmol/L or pH drops to 7.00 or lower. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

rows: Rapid dialytic clearance of accumulated lactate
Metformin is water-soluble with low protein binding
Efficient extracorporeal removal of circulating drug

steps.tx: **Therapeutic plasma exchange**, or **TPE**, is an **ASFA** Category **I** first-line treatment for **TTP** and for **anti-GBM** disease with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, because exchange removes the pathogenic antibody. In the 2023 ASFA update, ANCA-associated vasculitis with alveolar hemorrhage is Category III, so exchange is not established as routine care after PEXIVAS.

steps.tx: Extracorporeal clearance via **hemoperfusion** or hemodialysis is fundamentally **ineffective** for intoxicants possessing an extraordinarily large **volume of distribution** exceeding **2** to **3** L/kg, such as tricyclic antidepressants, digoxin, and chloroquine. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Dialyzable Toxins (Low Vd)
points: Protein binding: Low plasma protein binding
Molecular size: Small water-soluble molecules (< 500 Da)
Examples: Methanol, ethylene glycol, lithium, salicylates

right.title: Non-Dialyzable Toxins (High Vd)
points: Volume of distribution: High (> 2 to 3 L/kg)
Tissue sequestration: Extensive lipid and tissue binding
